name: Pricing Table
description: Pricing plans side by side with a monthly or yearly billing choice: a radio group drawn as a segmented control, prices and savings worked out from each plan's prices, calls to action that are links, and cards that wrap on their own.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a pricing section: plan cards with a monthly or yearly billing choice drawn as a segmented control over real radios, prices and savings worked out from each plan's prices, calls to action that are links named by their visible text, and cards that wrap on their own. Prices come from the project's billing system. Build on the project's card, button, and form components when it has suitable ones. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A billing choice that is a radio group drawn as a segmented control, shown by the script
Prices formatted for the currency and the locale, with the period written out
Savings worked out from the prices in the smallest unit and rounded down, never stored apart from them
Prices that match the restored choice after Back
Calls to action that are links, named by their visible text
Cards that wrap to fewer columns on their own
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the billing system and its price data, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has pricing cards or a plan picker, configure or extend them to meet this guide instead of building others, and keep their APIs.
2. Get the plans and their prices from the billing system, in the currency's smallest unit (featureSpec.dataContract).
3. Render the plans (featureSpec.screens) and, if they have yearly prices, the billing choice (frameworkPatterns.billingChoice).
4. Work out the prices and savings as implementationDetails.prices says, and add the calls to action (implementationDetails.callsToAction) and the feature lists (implementationDetails.features).
6. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, forced colors, and Back, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

featureSpec.goal: Help people compare plans, see what each costs per month or per year, and pick one, with prices that are exactly what the billing system charges and savings worked out from them.
userJourney: Someone reaches the pricing section and sees each plan's monthly price, what it includes, and its call to action
They choose Yearly: every plan shows its yearly price "per year" and its saving, such as "Save 19% compared with monthly"
They follow a plan's call to action, a link to its signup page that carries the chosen period
If they come back, the choice they made is still chosen, and the prices and links match it

screens.purpose: Show the plans side by side, with the billing choice above them.

ui.heading: The section's h2, such as "Pricing"
ui.billingChoice: A fieldset with the legend "Billing" and two radios, Monthly and Yearly, drawn as a segmented control; the Yearly label says the best saving
ui.planCards: An article per plan: its h3, a sentence on who it's for, the price and period, the saving when Yearly is chosen, one call to action, and the feature list

interactions.accessibilityNotes: The radio says its new state; no announcement is needed, since the prices change where people read them next.
After Back, the browser restores the checked radio without a change event; the prices and links follow it.
A plain link; its name starts with its visible text.

edgeCases: A plan without a fixed price ("Contact sales") is left out of the prices and the savings
A free plan (0 and 0) has nothing to save and is left out of the savings
Prices with cents keep them ("$9.99"); whole prices drop ".00"
Every plan saves the same: the Yearly label says "Save 17%", not "up to"
Two or four plans: the grid wraps on its own
A currency without cents (JPY): the smallest unit is the whole yen, which the formatter's fraction digits give
No yearly prices at all: leave the billing choice out
A promotion that ends: say its end date in text, with no countdown that pressures

billingPeriod.persistence: The checked radio, which the browser restores after Back; optionally the URL (?billing=yearly)

dataContract.plan: id, name, a sentence on who it's for, monthly and yearly prices in the smallest unit (absent for "Contact sales"), the currency, the signup link or a price id for each period, whether it's highlighted, and its features (name, included)
dataContract.source: The project's billing system; the page never computes a price the billing system doesn't charge

requirements.1.4.1: Included and not included features say so in text, not only with icons or color.
requirements.1.4.10: Cards wrap; nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide.
requirements.1.4.11: The segmented control's edge, the chosen option's marker, the focus ring, and meaningful icons meet 3:1.

requirements.2.4.7: The focused billing option shows a focus ring in every browser.

keyboardNavigation.order: The billing choice, then each plan's call to action, in the order on screen.
keyboardNavigation.billingChoice: One Tab stop; the arrows choose Monthly or Yearly.

featureList.aria-labelledby: The plan's heading, or a "Professional includes" heading

screenReader.billingChoice: Two options, Monthly and Yearly, are one choice: a radio group (<fieldset> with the <legend> "Billing"), drawn as a segmented control. The radios stay real: the group is one Tab stop, the arrows choose, and screen readers say something like "Yearly, radio button, 2 of 2". A switch would be read as "on" or "off" and can only name one side.
screenReader.prices: The period is written out, "per month" or "per year"; abbreviations are read letter by letter or as "slash mo". Say whether tax is included where that's required.
screenReader.features: Each plan's features are a list. A feature it doesn't include says so in text, such as a visually hidden "Not included:" before it, or the list holds only what's included, starting with "Everything in Starter, plus:".

focusManagement.billingChoice: The focused option shows a focus ring on :focus: WebKit doesn't match :focus-visible on a radio the arrows moved to (checked). In forced colors, which replace backgrounds, the chosen option takes the system's Highlight.

colorContrast.note: Colors: #111827 text (17.7:1 on white), #4b5563 muted text (7.6:1); a primary call to action in #2563eb with white text (5.2:1), since #3b82f6 is only 3.7:1; the segmented control's edge #6b7280 (4.8:1), the chosen option #111827 with white text, and a #2563eb focus ring. Check the project's own colors the same way.

cardHover.properties: box-shadow, and translate when motion is allowed

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, prices change at once and cards don't move.

designSystem.note: Suggested defaults for projects without a design. The project's tokens and existing components win.
designSystem.sizes: Cards with 24 to 40 px of padding and a 12 to 16 px radius; the plan's name 20 to 28 px; the price 40 to 56 px.
designSystem.colors: Colors: #111827 text (17.7:1 on white), #4b5563 muted text (7.6:1); a primary call to action in #2563eb with white text (5.2:1), since #3b82f6 is only 3.7:1; the segmented control's edge #6b7280 (4.8:1), the chosen option #111827 with white text, and a #2563eb focus ring. Check the project's own colors the same way.

implementationDetails.plans: Plans and prices come from the project's billing system (Stripe, Paddle, the app's own), with each price in the currency's smallest unit, such as cents. Prices are rendered on the server. Each plan is an <article> named by its heading (<h3> under the section's <h2>), with its price, a sentence on who it's for, one call to action, and what it includes. A "Most popular" badge is plain text, not a live region, and only on a plan that is the most popular. On phones, a plan shown first is first in the page too, not moved with CSS order, so the reading and focus order match what's shown.
implementationDetails.billing: Two options, Monthly and Yearly, are one choice: a radio group (<fieldset> with the <legend> "Billing"), drawn as a segmented control. The radios stay real: the group is one Tab stop, the arrows choose, and screen readers say something like "Yearly, radio button, 2 of 2". A switch would be read as "on" or "off" and can only name one side. Monthly is chosen by default, or whichever period the server renders. The Yearly option's label says the best saving ("Save up to 19%"), or the one saving when every plan saves the same ("Save 17%"). Without script the choice can't change the prices, so the server renders one period's prices and the script shows the choice. After Back, the browser restores the checked option without an input or change event, and Chromium does it only after the page's scripts and DOMContentLoaded have run (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Work the prices out from the checked option when the script runs and again on pageshow. The focused option shows a focus ring on :focus: WebKit doesn't match :focus-visible on a radio the arrows moved to (checked). In forced colors, which replace backgrounds, the chosen option takes the system's Highlight. Choosing needs no announcement: the radio says its new state, and the prices change where people read them next.
implementationDetails.prices: Prices are formatted with Intl.NumberFormat for the currency and the page's language; trailingZeroDisplay: "stripIfInteger" shows "$29" and "$9.99" (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The period is written out, "per month" or "per year"; abbreviations are read letter by letter or as "slash mo". Say whether tax is included where that's required. Savings are claims, so they come from the prices: (12 × monthly − yearly) ÷ (12 × monthly), worked out in the smallest unit, so a plan that saves exactly 20% says 20 (in floating point it comes out at 19.999…%), and rounded down, so they never claim more than a plan saves. The example plans save 17.6%, 19.8%, and 16.7%: "Save 17%", "Save 19%", and "Save 16%". Don't store a separate discount figure that can drift from the prices. A plan without a fixed price ("Contact sales") is left out of the calculation, and so is a free plan, which has nothing to save: dividing by its monthly price of 0 made the label "Save up to NaN%" (checked).
implementationDetails.callsToAction: Calls to action go to signup or checkout pages, so they're links, with no loading or disabled state of their own. The highlighted plan's is the primary one. They take the chosen period to signup: the script sets billing=yearly or billing=monthly on each plan's link (or the billing system's price id for that period), and the server renders the default period's links. Otherwise signup can't tell which price was chosen. Their visible text comes first in their name: "Get started", with "with Professional" visually hidden after it, so voice control users can say what they see (WCAG 2.5.3) and screen readers can tell them apart. "Start free trial" only on a plan with a trial; otherwise "Get started" or "Contact sales".
implementationDetails.features: Each plan's features are a list. A feature it doesn't include says so in text, such as a visually hidden "Not included:" before it, or the list holds only what's included, starting with "Everything in Starter, plus:". Check and cross icons are aria-hidden="true" and meet 3:1: a #047857 check is 5.5:1 on white and a #6b7280 cross 4.8:1, where #10b981 and #9ca3af are 2.5:1.
implementationDetails.layout: The cards wrap on their own with repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(16rem, 100%), 1fr)): three or four side by side on wide screens, two on a tablet, one on a phone, without a breakpoint. Three fixed columns at 768 px would leave cards about 230 px wide. Rows that line up across cards (the price, the call to action, the features) can use grid-template-rows: subgrid; it's optional. A full comparison is a real <table> with a column per plan and a row header per feature, as in the Data Table guide.
implementationDetails.motion: Motion is optional: prices can fade over 150 ms when they change, and cards can lift on hover. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing moves; prices change at once.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

billingChoice.description: The billing choice and the prices: real radios drawn as a segmented control (one Tab stop, the arrows choose, a focus ring on :focus, the chosen option highlighted in forced colors), shown by the script; prices formatted with Intl.NumberFormat from each plan's prices in cents, savings worked out in whole cents and rounded down with free plans left out, each call to action's link carrying the chosen period, all worked out again on pageshow; and cards that wrap with auto-fit.

must: Build on the project's card, button, and form components when they're suitable, and keep their APIs
Take plans and prices from the project's billing system, in the smallest unit
Work savings out from the prices, and round them down
Make the billing choice a radio group, and calls to action links that carry the chosen period
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Hardcode a saving, or store one apart from the prices
Make the billing choice a switch, or move a plan with CSS order
Give a call to action an aria-label that replaces its visible text
Add analytics, or any dependency, without asking
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Each plan is an article named by its heading, with its price, what it includes, and one call to action
The billing choice is a fieldset with a legend and two radios, drawn as a segmented control: one Tab stop, the arrows choose, and the focused option shows a focus ring in every browser
Without script, the page shows one period's prices and no choice
Choosing Yearly updates every plan's price and period at once; a plan without a fixed price is left alone
Prices are formatted for the currency and the locale, and periods are written out ("per month"), not abbreviated
Savings are worked out from the prices in the currency's smallest unit and rounded down, leaving out free plans; the Yearly label says "Save up to" the best one, or "Save" when all are equal
After Back, the prices and the links match the restored choice
Calls to action are links whose names start with their visible text, with the plan's name added out of sight, and they take the chosen period to signup
Included and not included features say so in text, and their icons are hidden from screen readers and meet 3:1
A "Most popular" badge is plain text, is true, and is not a live region
Cards wrap to fewer columns on their own, a plan shown first on phones comes first in the page, and nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide
In forced colors, the chosen billing option is still visible
Text meets 4.5:1, and the segmented control's edge and focus ring 3:1
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
